text.ja: CIP：値と勾配を運ぶ 原型のcubic-interpolated pseudo-particle（CIP）は場と空間微分を保持し、風上の3次分布を再構成します。広い族はconstrained interpolation profileとも呼ばれます。CIPノートは定速周期スカラー移流の原型多項式を実装し、値だけの線形補間と比較して、拡散、勾配輸送、振動、細分化、保存性を調べます。 解説章公開コード・データ / Public code and data 英語原文が更新されています。この日本語訳は旧版に対応します。 歴史的出典はTakewaki–Nishiguchi–Yabe（1985）、Yabe–Aoki（1991）です。Saito–Obase–Abe-Ouchi（2020）はCIP族の値・勾配発展と有理関数型を説明しますが、氷床応用とRCIPはこの多項式例とは別です。 特性線と追加の未知数# 定速aでは、 ft+afx=0,g=fx,gt+agx=0. です。到着点x_iから出発点x_d=x_i−a dtへ逆追跡し、古い風上区間のfとgをそこで補間します。gは独立した発展変数で、毎ステップ新しいfの差分に置き換えません。N節点のCIPは2N、線形比較はN個のスカラー未知数です。 変速では勾配方程式に伸長が入り、 gt+agx=−axg. です。ソース、速度変化、圧縮性には追加更新と特性線処理が必要です。a_x≠0ではトレーサーf_t+a f_x=0と保存密度f_t+(af)_x=0も異なります。初版は両形式が一致する定速だけを使います。 4つの端点条件で3次式を決める# 幅hの区間で規格化座標s∈[0,1]を使うと、 P(s)=H00(s)fL+hH10(s)gL+H01(s)fR+hH11(s)gR, H00=2s3−3s2+1,H10=s3−2s2+s,H01=−2s3+3s2,H11=s3−s2. です。端点値と物理微分を再現し、新状態はf_i=P(s_d)、g_i=P′(s_d)/hです。P′はsで微分します。正のaでは区間[x_{i−1},x_i]とs_d=1−a dt/h、負では[x_i,x_{i+1}]とs_d=−a dt/hです。出発点を隣接区間に収めるため|a|dt/h≤1とし、等号なら両配列を厳密に1節点移動します。 この定速問題に対する完全な特性線・再配置更新であり、任意のRKで進める空間右辺ではありません。RKの族に並ぶ方法で、その係数表の一員ではありません。一般の半Lagrange法は複数セルを越えられますが、この隣接セル例の範囲外です。 再現可能なスカラーテスト# 周期[0,1]にN=128の点x_i=i/Nを置きます。ノートはa=±1、Courant絶対値0.25、0.6、1、終了時刻0.25、1を選び、最終刻みを短縮します。設定ごとに終了時刻まで独立に解き、保存解間の補間はしません。 滑らかな分布は1+0.2sin(2πx)で、初期gは解析微分または周期中心差分です。矩形パルスは[0.2,0.4)で1、他で0、初期勾配はゼロまたは中心差分です。標本化した不連続でゼロを使うのは明示した規約で、そこでの解析微分ではないため、矩形波の厳密勾配誤差は表示しません。 参照fは厳密に移動した点値標本で、有限体積勾配制限ノートのセル平均とは異なります。L1は平均絶対点誤差です。初期勾配の選択は急峻な分布へ大きく影響し得ます。基本3次式にTVD・単調性・正値性の制限はなく、矩形波に過大・過小値が現れます。線形比較は同じ符号付き特性線の点値更新で、|C|≤1では1次風上と代数的に同じです。 滑らかな解の細分化はN=32、64、128、256、a=1、Courant=0.6、T=0.37です。両勾配初期化で値誤差は3次へ近づき、勾配誤差は別に記録します。3次補間だけで反復再配置後の大域4次精度を主張できません。整数Courantは特殊な厳密移動なので一般次数の推定には使いません。N状態の線形法と2N状態のCIPに同一コストの順位も付けません。 正弦波だけでは保存性を証明できない# 周期区分Hermite再構成の厳密積分は、 M=∑i[h2(fi+fi+1)+h212(gi−gi+1)]=h∑ifi. です。一様・定速で割合sだけ再配置すると、1ステップ変化は、 ΔM=h2 [H10(s)+H11(s)]∑igi. です。解析的正弦勾配と中心差分の初期和はゼロなので、一般の保存的再配置性がなくても、表示スカラー例は積分を丸め誤差まで保つ場合があります。 別の反例は、N=32、全節点でf_i=1、g_i=1の正当な周期C1 Hermite場です。これは定数関数ではありません。各区間に小さな3次波形があり、節点間で微分が変わります。厳密積分は1で、厳密移動はそれを保ちますが、C=0.35の1回のCIP再配置は、 s=0.65,ΔM=h s(1−s)(1−2s)=−0.0021328125. を与えます。最初の4区間で、元の再構成の厳密移動とCIP場を比べます。性質の主張を検証するため意図的に作った格子スケールの例で、すべての滑らかな流れの質量誤差予測ではありません。粗い求積ではなく解析積分を使います。容易な問題の小誤差から、より強い保証は導けません。 保存型・形状保存型の分岐# CIP–CSL（Yabeら、2001）は積分制約と保存的半Lagrange輸送を導入します。有理CIP／RCIPは再構成を変え、別の変種は形状制約を加えます。保存性と有界性には独自の定義とテストが必要で、CIPという名称だけからは導けません。 初版は原型の1次元3次式だけを実装します。CIP–CSL2／CSL4、RCIP、流体の移流・非移流分割、多次元混合微分、完全な圧縮性・多相ソルバーは読書の背景です。既存Euler衝撃波管の再構成と流束は変更していません。 再現# from numart.cip import solve_advection, mass_counterexample wave = solve_advection(profile="sine", speed=-1., cfl=0.6) pulse = solve_advection(profile="square", gradient="centered") print(mass_counterexample()["mass_after"]) python scripts/build_cip.py python scripts/sync_web_content.py docs/figures/cip.jsonはCIP／線形の48組の設定、微分配列、診断、3つの収束系列、保存性反例、ソースハッシュを記録します。ブラウザーはPython計算結果を選びます。テストでは3次再構成・微分の厳密性、両方向、1セル移動、定数保存、滑らかな収束、振動、解析的質量変化の恒等式を確認します。 歴史アトラス →計算結果のギャラリー →
text.en: CIP: carry the value and the gradient The original cubic-interpolated pseudo-particle (CIP) idea stores a field and its spatial derivative, then reconstructs an upwind cubic profile. The broader family is also called constrained interpolation profile. The CIP notebook implements the original polynomial construction for constant-speed periodic scalar advection. It compares value-only linear interpolation with CIP and checks diffusion, gradient transport, oscillations, refinement, and conservation. THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Historical references are Takewaki–Nishiguchi–Yabe (1985) and Yabe–Aoki (1991). The accessible Saito–Obase–Abe-Ouchi (2020) paper describes CIP-family value/gradient evolution and a rational variant; its ice-sheet application and RCIP algorithm are separate from this polynomial example. Characteristics and an additional unknown# For constant velocity a, ft+afx=0,g=fx,gt+agx=0. At a receiving point x_i, trace backward to x_d=x_i−a dt. Interpolate both f and g from the old upwind interval at that departure point. The evolved g is an independent state variable; it is not replaced after each step by a finite difference of the updated f. For N nodes, CIP therefore stores 2N scalar unknowns, while the linear comparison stores N. For variable velocity the gradient equation instead includes stretching: gt+agx=−axg. Source terms, velocity variation, and compressibility require additional updates and characteristic treatment. A transported tracer f_t+a f_x=0 and a conserved density f_t+(af)_x=0 also differ when a_x is nonzero. This edition uses constant a only, where the two PDE forms coincide. Four endpoint constraints determine a cubic# On an interval of width h, with normalized coordinate s∈[0,1], the cubic is P(s)=H00(s)fL+hH10(s)gL+H01(s)fR+hH11(s)gR, H00=2s3−3s2+1,H10=s3−2s2+s,H01=−2s3+3s2,H11=s3−s2. The endpoint values and physical derivatives are reproduced, and the new states are f_i=P(s_d) and g_i=P′(s_d)/h. Here P′ differentiates with respect to s. For positive a, the interval is [x_{i−1},x_i] and s_d=1−a dt/h; for negative a it is [x_i,x_{i+1}] and s_d=−a dt/h. The implementation restricts |a|dt/h≤1 to keep the departure point in this adjacent interval. The case |a|dt/h=1 shifts both arrays by one node exactly. This is a complete characteristic/remapping update for this constant-speed problem, rather than a spatial RHS subsequently advanced by an arbitrary RK method. It belongs beside the RK family, not inside its list of time-integration tableaus. More general semi-Lagrangian schemes can cross multiple cells; that capability is outside this adjacent-cell example. Reproducible scalar tests# The domain is periodic [0,1], with N=128 point nodes x_i=i/N. Notebook choices are a=±1, Courant magnitudes 0.25, 0.6, or 1, and final times 0.25 or 1. The last step is shortened. Every configuration is solved independently to its selected final time, without interpolation between saved solutions. The smooth profile is 1+0.2 sin(2πx). Initial g is either its analytic derivative or the centered periodic difference. The square pulse is one on [0.2,0.4) and zero elsewhere. Its initial slopes are either zero or centered differences. Zero is an explicit convention at a sampled discontinuity, not an analytic derivative there. Consequently there is no square-pulse exact gradient error displayed. The reference f is exact translated point samples. These are not the cell-average references used in the finite-volume limiter notebook. Reported L1 means the average absolute point error. Initial-gradient choice can materially affect sharp features. The basic cubic has no TVD, monotonicity, or positivity limiter, and the square test shows overshoot and undershoot. The linear interpolation comparison is the same signed-characteristic point-value update, algebraically first-order upwind for |C|≤1. Smooth refinement uses N=32,64,128,256, a=1, Courant=0.6, and T=0.37. The computed value errors approach order three for both gradient initializations; the gradient errors are recorded separately. A cubic interpolant alone is not a fourth-order global-accuracy claim after repeated remapping. Integer Courant shifts are a special exact-translation case, so they are not used to infer a generic refinement order. No equal-cost ranking is made between the N-state linear method and the 2N-state CIP method. Why a sine wave is not a conservation proof# The exact integral of the periodic piecewise-Hermite reconstruction is M=∑i[h2(fi+fi+1)+h212(gi−gi+1)]=h∑ifi. For uniform constant-speed remapping with fraction s, its one-step change is ΔM=h2 [H10(s)+H11(s)]∑igi. The initial analytic sine slopes and centered differences sum to zero, so the displayed scalar runs can conserve this integral to roundoff even though the method has no universal conservative remapping property. The separate counterexample uses N=32 and a valid periodic C1 Hermite field with f_i=1 and g_i=1 at every node. This is not a constant function: each interval contains a small cubic ripple, and its derivative varies between the nodes. Its exact integral is 1. Exact translation preserves that integral, while one CIP remapping step at C=0.35 gives s=0.65,ΔM=h s(1−s)(1−2s)=−0.0021328125. The plot shows the exact shifted original reconstruction and the reconstructed CIP field over the first four intervals. This is an intentionally constructed grid-scale test of a claimed property, not a prediction of the mass error for every smooth flow. Integrals are evaluated analytically, not by coarse quadrature. Small errors in an easy test cannot establish a stronger guarantee. Conservative and shape-preserving branches# CIP–CSL (Yabe et al., 2001) introduces an integral constraint and conservative semi-Lagrangian transport. Rational CIP / RCIP changes the reconstruction, and variants apply additional shape constraints. Conservation and boundedness require their own definitions and tests; neither follows solely from the CIP name. This edition implements the original 1D cubic only. CIP–CSL2/CSL4, RCIP, fluid advection/non-advection splitting, multidimensional mixed derivatives, and complete compressible or multiphase solvers are reading context. The existing Euler shock-tube solvers retain their documented reconstruction and flux choices. Reproduce# from numart.cip import solve_advection, mass_counterexample wave = solve_advection(profile="sine", speed=-1., cfl=0.6) pulse = solve_advection(profile="square", gradient="centered") print(mass_counterexample()["mass_after"]) python scripts/build_cip.py python scripts/sync_web_content.py docs/figures/cip.json records 48 paired CIP/linear configurations, derivative arrays, diagnostics, three refinement series, the conservation counterexample, and source hashes. The browser selects these Python-computed results. Tests check exact cubic reconstruction and derivatives, both directions, one-cell shifts, constant preservation, smooth refinement, oscillations, and the analytic mass-change identity.
